In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AvrRpts2 reporter is a useful tool for identifying effectors in culture and in planta.
bioinformatic prediction of P. syringa T3SS effectors is correct for most effectors but that some predicted effectors may be secreted via a different secretion system.
the AvrRPT2(81-250) reporter is not a T3SS substrate but rather a reporter of the N-terminal regions of P. syringaevirulence proteins that are important for protein accumulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a positive serine-bias in N-terminal regions is a useful bioinformatic feature for predicting P. syring ae and P. fluoresc ens effectors.
the hrp box and the N-terminal region of P. syringaeclassical and nonclassical effectors can be used to identify effectors.
a positive serine N-terminal bias is a common feature of many P. syringa e effectors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hrp box and N-terminal amino acid bias are useful features for bioinformatic prediction of Pseudomonas effectors.
a serine-rich region of the N-termini of P. syringaee effectors may not be essential for their secretion but may be important for their accumulation in bacteria.
the hrp box and N-terminal region biases of effectors can be used to predict many effectors in the plant pathogenic and nonpathogenic Pseudomonas species.
